clue.text: Writer's block finally disappeared

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is': the writer is what the wordplay gives, J. M. of Peter Pan fame

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for block has vanished, so its closing R is dropped

parts.note: a barrier is a block, something that obstructs the way

explanation.surface: An author's creative drought has at last lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's block' is one phrase in the surface but splits in two: the writer is the definition and 'block' alone is a synonym to be shortened. 'finally disappeared' removes its last letter, R.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie, the Scottish author of Peter Pan, is an example of a novelist and playwright.

clue.text: Secure piano in middle of jetty for musician

parts.note: to bag something is to secure or obtain it

indicators.note: the letter for piano goes into the centre of the word for jetty

parts.note: a pier is a jetty, a structure built out over water
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: Someone fastens down a piano halfway along a landing stage so a performer can play it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secure' reads as fasten down but means obtain; 'in middle of' asks for the piano's letter at the very centre of the jetty, not anywhere inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the Scottish pipes is one kind of instrumentalist, so this is definition by example.

clue.text: Offered lots of education reforms

indicators.note: as a verb, to re-form is to shape again, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A government put forward a great many changes to schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' looks like 'many' but means the items in a sale; 'reforms' is the anagram signal working on 'education'.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold at a sale by bidding are divided into numbered lots, so putting lots up for sale is exactly this verb.

clue.text: As patient, perhaps, attending doctor's practice

indicators.note: the word for being unwell stands next to, in attendance on, the doctor's abbreviation, coming after it

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
a patient is typically ill, so 'as a patient may be' describes being unwell

explanation.surface: Someone goes along to their GP's surgery as one of the sick.
explanation.walkthrough: A doctor's practice is the surgery in the surface, but 'practice' alone is the definition, meaning repeated training. 'attending' places ILL beside DR.
explanation.definitionFit: Repetitive training exercises are a synonym for rehearsal, as in a fire rehearsal or military square-bashing.

clue.text: Like a plane that's also down in time when redirected

indicators.note: sending something in a new direction rearranges it, so the letters of the four words before are reordered

explanation.surface: An aircraft that was diverted still managed to land punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: The plane is a flat geometric surface, not an aircraft. 'when redirected' rearranges ALSO DOWN IN TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric plane is flat, having length and breadth but no depth, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Thrash learner, beset by bad exam result

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded, so the learner's letter sits within the word for a bad result

parts.note: a fail is the worst outcome of an examination
L is the abbreviation for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A student gets a beating after being dogged by a poor mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beset by' puts L inside FAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat or swing wildly, a near synonym; the noun is a threshing tool, and thresh is a variant of the same verb.

clue.text: Part of issue clear always, poetically, for Shakespeare, say

parts.note: issue means offspring, and a son is one of someone's children
to net or to clear a sum is to earn it after deductions
e'er is the poets' shortening of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: One section of a magazine is forever lucid and lyrical to a reader like the Bard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' is offspring rather than an edition, and 'clear' is the earnings sense. 'say' marks Shakespeare as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote 154 fourteen-line poems, so he is a famous example of a writer of that verse form.

clue.text: Cafe in Paris is a money-maker, pulling in English

parts.note: est is the French word for 'is'

indicators.note: the money-maker draws the letter for English inside itself

parts.note: a mint is the place where coins are made

explanation.surface: A coffee house in the French capital earns a fortune by attracting British tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris is' means the French for 'is', leaving 'Cafe' alone as the definition. 'pulling in' puts E inside MINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A French word for a small bar or bistro serving drinks and coffee, a synonym borrowed into English.

clue.text: Measurement of circumference hard area of maths? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the opposite way round: the two pieces joined in clue order are then read from right to left

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
trig, short for trigonometry, is a branch of mathematics

explanation.surface: Is working out the distance round a circle the tough part of mathematics? No, quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' usually swaps container and contents; here it turns the whole of H plus TRIG backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance round something, such as a waist or a tree trunk, is a synonym.

clue.text: Group of artists spoiled atelier, perhaps

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined or broken up, so the letters of the two words after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A band of painters may have wrecked a studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' rearranges ATELIER PERHAPS; 'perhaps' is fodder, not a hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian brotherhood of Rossetti, Millais and Holman Hunt is an example of a painters' movement.

clue.text: Island area, sound as a bell

parts.note: to toll is to ring slowly, the sound a bell makes

explanation.surface: A stretch of an isle is in perfectly good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound as a bell' is an idiom for healthy, but here it literally means to ring as a bell does.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a lagoon is one kind of isle.

clue.text: Higher still in former scale — or replacing us

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner

indicators.note: the clue spells out the swap: within the name of the scale, the letters 'or' take the place of the letters 'us'

parts.note: Celsius is the temperature scale

explanation.surface: Notes climb further up an old musical scale, or one that is taking our place.
explanation.walkthrough: The scale is one of temperature, not music, and 'or replacing us' is a literal instruction about its letters rather than a second alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin comparative meaning 'ever upward', used as a motto, as in Longfellow's poem.

clue.text: Surpassing in storytelling? Not close

definitions.meaning: a whimsical verb for beating someone at telling untruths, as outrunning is beating them at running
remote, far from the centre, as of distant districts

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words joined it would mean beating another at fibbing; as an adjective it means remote from the centre.

clue.text: Author adding another zero — this has a lot of them

definitions.text: this has a lot of them

indicators.note: one more round letter is put into the author's name, which already has two

parts.note: Nikolai Gogol was the Russian author of Dead Souls
the letter O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: A writer tacks one more nought onto a figure that already has plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' refers back to zeros. 'adding' slips a third O into GOGOL.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the number ten to the power of a hundred, written as a one followed by a hundred noughts.

clue.text: In a blissful state outside university, looking much better

indicators.note: the word for blessed goes round the university letter

parts.note: beatified means made blessedly happy, or declared blessed by the Church

explanation.surface: Away from campus, someone is blissfully happy and has a far healthier appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps BEATIFIED round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made lovelier has had its appearance improved, a paraphrase of the participle.

clue.text: Page 3, for example, clergyman clipped?

indicators.note: clipping trims the end off, so the cleric loses his last letter

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest in the Church of England

explanation.surface: A vicar has been cut out of a tabloid's notorious topless-model page.
explanation.walkthrough: Page 3 was the Sun newspaper's topless-model page, but here it is simply an odd-numbered, right-hand page. 'clipped' drops the last R.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd-numbered pages fall on the right-hand side of an open book, which is what this printing term names.

clue.text: First make a minimal subscription?

definitions.meaning: the adjective meaning at the very beginning
to subscribe is literally to write underneath, to sign; the shortest way to sign is with the first letters of your name

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means earliest; as a verb it means to sign a document with just the first letters of one's name.

clue.text: You'll find some of Incan descent here

indicators.note: only part of the two words that follow is wanted, a run of letters across the gap between them

explanation.surface: In this region live a few people whose ancestors were Incas.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the place: 'some of' takes a run from 'Incan descent', and descendants of the Incas really do live there.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American mountain range was the heartland of the Inca empire, so the entire clue points to it.

clue.text: Innkeeper's secretary with buzzer that doesn't work

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is': an Italian landlord is what the pieces make

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
a drone is a male bee, which buzzes but does no work in the hive

explanation.surface: A landlord's assistant is stuck with a broken doorbell.
explanation.walkthrough: The buzzer is not a faulty doorbell but a male bee, which famously does no work.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian word for a master or proprietor, used in English especially for the landlord of an inn.

clue.text: Fellow crossing river on one large vessel, a warship

indicators.note: the word for fellow stretches across the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a peer is an equal, a fellow

indicators.note: in a down clue the river's letter sits on top of the letter for one

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
I is the Roman numeral for one
a vat is a big container for liquid

explanation.surface: A chap goes over a waterway aboard a big ship, a naval one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' appears to be the ship of the surface but is a container for liquid; the real ship is the definition, and 'crossing' makes the fellow span everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A privately owned armed ship licensed by a government to attack enemy shipping, so a kind of fighting vessel.

clue.text: Bank seldom sending away artist

indicators.note: the letters for artist are dismissed from the word for seldom

parts.note: rarely means seldom, not often
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A financial institution hardly ever turns a painter from its door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is the verb, as in 'bank on someone'. 'sending away' removes RA from RARELY.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on someone is to depend on them, so the verbs are synonyms, each followed by 'on'.

clue.text: Improperly spurn one political outcast

indicators.note: done improperly means not in the right way, so the letters of the two words after it are disordered

explanation.surface: The party wrongly rejects a single exiled dissident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Improperly' rearranges SPURN ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's term in Nineteen Eighty-Four for someone erased from the record for ideological reasons.

clue.text: Examination covering right part of body for a lot of players

indicators.note: the word for an exam wraps round the other two pieces

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
the chest is the front of the upper torso

explanation.surface: A team doctor's check-up takes in the correct bit of anatomy for most of the squad.
explanation.walkthrough: The players are musicians, not sportsmen, and 'covering' wraps the exam round the other pieces, which keep the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Music scored for a full symphonic ensemble is written for many instrumentalists, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: For mates at sea, time to get behind all on board

indicators.note: to be at sea is to be confused or lost, so the letters of the two words before it are mixed

explanation.surface: For the ship's officers on a voyage, the moment has come to back the whole crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get behind' in the surface means support, but 'behind' is positional and belongs to the definition; 'at sea' is the anagram signal, with the letter for time added last.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical superlative meaning nearest the stern, so further back than everything else on a ship.

clue.text: Bird you finally found nesting in new roof

indicators.note: the single letter settles inside the other pieces as a bird sits in a nest

parts.note: thatch is a roof covering of straw or reed

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word before it is used

explanation.surface: At last you discover a feathered creature building its home in the fresh housetop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the U of 'you', and 'found nesting in' puts it inside N plus THATCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A small woodland species that climbs head-first down tree trunks, so an example of the class.

clue.text: Doctor stands over recovery, in ethical way

indicators.note: in a down clue the doctor's letters stand above the word for recovery

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor in the forces
a rally is a recovery, as when prices or a patient pick up

explanation.surface: A physician watches closely as a patient gets better, behaving with proper principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stands over' places MO above RALLY in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb synonym: acting with regard to right and wrong.

clue.text: Scientist as person with convictions upset one Pope

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue, so the word for a convict is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a lag is British slang for a habitual prisoner, someone convicted many times
I is the Roman numeral for one
Leo is the name of fourteen popes

explanation.surface: A man of science with firm beliefs annoyed a pontiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convictions' are criminal ones, not beliefs: 'upset' turns LAG into GAL. The surface recalls the astronomer's trial by the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian astronomer and physicist is a famous example, and he did fall foul of the papacy.

clue.text: Alternating with articles, write song of praise

indicators.note: completes the phrase 'alternating with': the second article goes into the next gap in the word for write
the letters of the word for write take turns with the two articles, so the first article goes between its first and second letters

parts.note: to pen something is to write it
A is the indefinite article; the plural asks for it twice, this being the first
the second of the two indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Between magazine pieces, a journalist composes a hymn of tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternating with' is one instruction: the letters of the word for write take turns with two indefinite articles. The articles are grammatical ones, not journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn of thanksgiving or triumph, originally addressed to Apollo, so a synonym.

clue.text: Article lacking substance, leader in Guardian

parts.note: thin means flimsy, without much body or weight

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word that follows is taken

explanation.surface: An insubstantial piece runs as the editorial in a national newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: A leader is a British newspaper's editorial; here 'leader in' takes the first letter of 'Guardian'. 'Article' means an object.
explanation.definitionFit: An object or item, as in 'an article of clothing', is a synonym.

clue.text: Foreign food cooked, initially, in Asian way

indicators.note: the single letter is placed inside the word for the Asian way

parts.note: Tao is the Chinese philosophical term meaning 'the way'

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word before it is used

explanation.surface: A dish from abroad is at first prepared in an oriental style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the C of 'cooked', and 'in' puts it inside TAO.
explanation.definitionFit: A folded Mexican tortilla with a filling is an example of a dish from overseas.
